Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The input contains two distinct proteomics contexts: one in the publication text describing global proteome analysis of YST-R tissues (LFQ, DDA), and one in the PRIDE metadata describing a Co-IP experiment for CD24 interaction partners. Both utilize LFQ and DDA (Shotgun). The PRIDE metadata explicitly labels the experiment as 'Affinity purification coupled with mass spectrometry proteomics', triggering the mod_ap_ms hint.

scope: co-immunoprecipitations of CD24 were performed in GCT, UC, PC, and RCC cell lines

Co-immunoprecipitations (Co-IP) were performed according to the manufacturer’s protocol by using 3 mg ‘Dynabeads M-270 Epoxy Beads’ (Thermo Fisher Scientific) coupled to 18 µg CD24 (SWA11) antibody or IgG2a isotype control

Upon elution in 1 x sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) buffer (30 % glycerin, 12 % SDS, 150 mM Tris Base in H2O, pH 7.0) at 37 °C for 20 minutes on a rocking platform, samples were further subjected to LC-MS.

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The PRIDE metadata explicitly describes the mass spectrometry material as the result of co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) of CD24, which constitutes an affinity-purified complex.

Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: The proteomics analysis (LC-MS) specifically compared primary (therapy-naïve) yolk-sac tumors (YST) against resistant yolk-sac tumors (YST-R) to identify markers of therapy resistance. While the study also describes drug screening (CLDN6-ADC, multikinase inhibitors), those were performed via XTT/flow cytometry and phospho-kinase arrays, not the primary LC-MS proteome analysis described in the results section (Fig 4).
